My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know what works here. The soil is good flat ground on the North China Plain, and there is only one system that makes sense: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same field. I have done this rotation my whole life. Eight mu of land, same as always.

I plant the wheat in early October after the maize comes off. I buy improved seeds from the village supply shop — the old varieties I used to save myself don't yield as well anymore, and everyone here switched years ago. I put down compound fertilizer when I plant, then urea in spring when the wheat greens up after the cold. I water four times: once before winter to protect the roots, once in late February when growth starts again, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in November and then fungicide and insecticide before the ears fill out. I use the rotary tiller before planting wheat — the soil has to be prepared properly.

After wheat harvest in June I plant the maize immediately. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or whatever the shop has this year. The rains usually come in July and August so I may only need to water once, maybe twice if it is dry. I apply fertilizer twice — compound at planting and urea when the plant is knee-high. No need to till, I plant directly into the stubble. Two pesticide sprays, one early for pests, one for disease near tasseling.

I am not going to change this. My neighbors do the same. My father did the same. The land gives a reliable income this way.
